extras.label: Sasha
extras.sketch: late twenties, quick, protective of her friends, reads people fast
extras.speech: Dry, sarcastic valley cadence; reads people fast and says so.

extras.label: Marco
extras.sketch: easygoing on the surface, competitive underneath, likes an audience
extras.speech: Full frat-bro energy in small doses: 'bro', 'let's go', 'no shot', loud and quick.

extras.label: Nina
extras.sketch: fifties, warm but sharp, asks the question everyone else avoids
extras.speech: Unhurried and warm with an edge; asks the question nobody else will.

floors.title: Last call at the bar
floors.blurb: She's interested until her friend shows up.
floors.setting: A crowded bar, Friday, 12:40am. You've been talking to Ines by the bar for a few minutes. It's loud enough that you have to lean in.
floors.opener: Okay wait, say that again, I literally couldn't hear you.

roles.Sasha: Ines's best friend, here to check on her
roles.Marco: a guy at the bar who knows Ines from work

beats: Ines asks him something oddly specific about what he just said, to see if there's anything behind it.
Sasha walks up, looks him up and down, and asks Ines if she's okay. Then asks him directly who he is.
Sasha asks what he does, and doesn't let him get away with a vague answer.
Marco slides in, greets Ines a little too familiarly, and offers to buy both girls a drink. Ignores him.
Ines says she should probably get back to her friends, watching how he reacts.
Last call is announced. Ines asks, half-joking, what he's doing after this.

floors.title: Friend-of-a-friend party
floors.blurb: You know one person. He just left you with strangers.
floors.setting: A house party in a small apartment. Dev, the only person you know, drags you into a group in the kitchen.
floors.opener: Guys, this is the one I told you about. Okay, go, tell them the thing.

roles.Marco: Dev's roommate, opinionated, holds court in the kitchen
roles.Sasha: a girl in the group who's funny and a little mean

beats: Dev leaves to get the door, abandoning him with Marco and Sasha. Marco asks how he knows Dev.
Sasha asks a playfully loaded question: hot take, what's something everyone here likes that he thinks is overrated.
Marco disagrees with his take, loudly, with a bad argument, playing to the room.
An awkward silence lands. Nobody fills it. Let it sit one beat, then Sasha raises an eyebrow at him.
Dev comes back and puts him on the spot to tell an embarrassing story about Dev to the group.
Sasha says she's heading to another party and asks if he wants to come, in front of Marco.

floors.title: Dinner with her parents
floors.blurb: Her dad is polite. That's the problem.
floors.setting: Dinner at your partner's parents' house. She stepped out to take a call. It's you, her dad Julian, and her mom Nina.
floors.opener: So. She tells us you're doing something with startups now.

roles.Nina: her mom, kind, curious, asks the real questions

beats: Nina asks how they met, and wants the real version, not the cute one.
Julian asks what he actually earns from it, framed politely but meaning it.
Julian makes a mildly loaded political comment and waits to see if he agrees.
Nina mentions, casually, that her ex used to come to these dinners too, and how much Julian liked him.
Julian asks where he sees this going with their daughter. Specifically. Timeline.
Julian asks him to help with the dishes, alone, and goes quiet in a way that's clearly a test.

floors.title: The interview turns
floors.blurb: First round went fine. Then a second person joins.
floors.setting: A final-round interview at a company you actually want. Julian, the hiring manager, has been friendly so far.
floors.opener: Walk me through the gap on your CV. The eight months.

roles.Nina: the VP, joins late, distracted, decisive

beats: Julian pushes on the weakest-sounding part of his last answer: meaning what, specifically.
Nina, the VP, walks in late, apologises to nobody, and asks him to summarise himself in thirty seconds.
Nina asks for his salary expectation, a number, now.
Julian asks about a time he was clearly wrong and someone else was right.
Nina says, flatly, that they have a strong internal candidate, and asks why they should take the risk on him.
Julian asks if he has any questions for them, and it's obvious a weak question will hurt.

floors.title: The bill arrives
floors.blurb: Marco ordered the steak and three cocktails.
floors.setting: Group dinner for Dev's birthday at a nice place. You had a salad and water. Marco ordered the steak, wine and three cocktails.
floors.opener: Okay, bill's here. Easiest thing is we just split it four ways, yeah?

roles.Marco: ordered the most, acting like it's nothing
roles.Sasha: also ate light, watching to see if anyone says something

beats: Marco says splitting evenly is the only non-annoying way and anyone who itemises is cheap.
Sasha, quietly, looks at him to see if he'll say it so she doesn't have to.
Marco realises he left his card in the car and asks him to cover him, he'll send it later.
Dev, a bit drunk, says it's his birthday and he shouldn't have to pay at all, half-joking, waiting for someone to agree.
Three days later: Marco still hasn't paid him back. Marco texts, read aloud: 'yo what do I owe you again lol'.
Marco gets defensive when pressed and says he's being weird about money.

floors.title: The roommate talk
floors.blurb: Rent is late. Again. Her boyfriend basically lives here.
floors.setting: Your shared kitchen, 11pm. Kai's rent share is a week late for the third month. Kai's partner has been staying over most nights.
floors.opener: You've been weird all day. If you've got something to say, say it.

roles.Marco: Kai's partner, who is very much here right now

beats: Kai gets defensive and points out something he does that's also annoying, specific and slightly true.
Marco wanders into the kitchen in a towel, says hey, and opens the fridge. Eats his food.
Kai says Marco being here basically saves them both money because he buys groceries sometimes.
Kai goes quiet and says things have been hard lately, money-wise. It might be real, might be a deflection.
Kai asks if he's saying he wants Kai to move out.
Kai proposes a deal that's slightly unfair to him and waits.

floors.title: The date that's slipping
floors.blurb: Great first ten minutes. Then her phone buzzes.
floors.setting: A first date at a small wine bar. It started well. Her phone has buzzed twice.
floors.opener: Sorry, sorry. Okay. Where were we, you were saying something about your job?

roles.Nina: the server, friendly, a little nosy

beats: Mara asks him what he'd do if money didn't matter, and doesn't accept a generic answer.
The server, Nina, interrupts to ask if they want another bottle, and says to Mara 'oh you're back!' in a way that implies she's been here on dates before.
Mara brings up her ex, unprompted, in a way that's a little too detailed.
Mara asks him what his last relationship taught him, eyes on him.
Her phone buzzes again. She looks at it, then at him, and asks if he minds if she answers it.
The bill comes. Mara asks, lightly, whether he'd want to do this again. She's hard to read.

floors.title: Working the room
floors.blurb: One shot at the person who can hire you.
floors.setting: A rooftop industry event. Theo, a senior person at a firm you want to join, is alone for a second with a drink.
floors.opener: Let me guess. You're here to network.

roles.Marco: a loud guy from a rival firm who dominates conversations
roles.Nina: a partner at Theo's firm, the actual decision maker

beats: Theo asks why that firm, specifically, and says everyone gives the same answer.
Marco barges in, talks over him about his own deal, and tries to pull Theo away.
Theo asks him a sharp technical or opinion question in front of Marco, to see who has a real view.
Nina walks up. Theo introduces him and Nina asks what he'd change about their firm.
Nina has to leave and asks for the one-line version of why she should remember him.
Theo says he's going to get another drink, which is an exit. See if he lets it end well.

floors.title: The morning after
floors.blurb: Her roommate is in the kitchen. So is the question.
floors.setting: Mara's apartment, 9am. You stayed over after a night out. Coffee in the kitchen. Things were great last night. Now it's daylight.
floors.opener: Morning. So. That happened. Coffee? It's terrible, fair warning.

roles.Sasha: Mara's roommate, walks in, unbothered, enjoying this a lot

beats: Mara teases him about something specific he said last night that he probably doesn't remember.
Sasha walks in, clocks him, says 'oh, hi' with a huge grin, and asks if he's the one from Thursday.
Sasha asks, deadpan, how he takes his coffee and whether he's staying for breakfast or 'doing the thing where you leave'.
Mara asks, half-joking, how many people he's brought home this month.
Mara says she's not really looking for anything serious right now, watching his face.
Mara asks if he wants to get food sometime, sober, or if this was just a thing.

floors.title: Wingman down
floors.blurb: Dev is crashing and taking you with him.
floors.setting: A rooftop bar. Dev is your wingman. He's three drinks deep and just walked you both up to Sasha and her friend.
floors.opener: Ladies. My boy here has a question for you. Go on. Ask them.

roles.Sasha: unimpressed, funny, testing both of them

beats: Sasha says 'he has a question? cute' and waits, arms crossed.
Dev tells an embarrassing story about him that is definitely exaggerated.
Sasha asks him to rate Dev's approach out of ten, honestly, in front of Dev.
Dev hits on Sasha badly and she shuts him down. Now it's awkward and on him to rescue it.
Sasha asks what his actual game is, since Dev's is clearly nonexistent.
Sasha gives him her Instagram but not her number and watches what he does with that.
